  "text": "He drew the lace through, then left the ends lying on the stone.

“You always did them too tight,” she said.

“I thought they came loose.”

“They did.”

The ferryman folded his cloth. There were crumbs on his coat, and he brushed them into his palm before standing.

Mara tied the shoe herself. When she looked up, Elias had moved a little way along the bank.

“Your watch,” he said.

She had forgotten it. The glass was clouded, though she had not put it in the river. She wiped it against her skirt.

“It's stopped.”

“It used to do that.”

“Only when you forgot.”

He put his hands in his pockets.

Across the water, a branch shook. She waited for the white thing to show itself again, but nothing came out from behind the leaves.

“Is someone waiting for you?”

“The boat is.”

“That isn't what I asked.”

“I know.”

The ferryman stepped aboard. Water entered around his boot and settled there. He made no effort to tip it out.

Mara fastened the watch around her wrist. The strap had dried stiff, and she used the next hole instead of the usual one.

They walked toward the path together. At the first rise she reached back, not looking, and found his sleeve. She held it between two fingers.

“The gate's farther than you remember,” she said.

They passed the place where she had left her basket. Rain had collected in a cabbage leaf inside it. Elias bent to lift the handle, but she took it before he could.

“Leave me something to carry.”"
